questions.question: In multi-clock domain digital IC design, why does a standard two-flip-flop synchronizer effectively mitigate metastability when passing a slow, single-bit control signal across asynchronous clock domains?
options: It provides an entire destination clock cycle for any metastable state induced in the first flip-flop to settle to a valid logic level before being sampled by the second flip-flop.
It converts multi-bit asynchronous bus data into Gray code to eliminate combinatorial glitches at the clock boundary.
It phase-aligns the transmitting and receiving clocks using an embedded delay-locked loop (DLL).
It dynamically stretches the destination clock pulse width whenever setup violations are detected.
It filters out high-frequency electromagnetic interference (EMI) using active capacitive decoupling.

questions.question: In synchronous digital integrated circuit design and Static Timing Analysis (STA), what is the fundamental conceptual distinction between 'clock skew' and 'clock jitter'?
options: Clock skew describes changes in clock frequency across supply voltage drops, while clock jitter describes static routing mismatches.

Clock skew is the spatial variation in arrival times of a clock edge across different physical locations, whereas clock jitter is the temporal variation in arrival times of clock edges at a single physical point over time.
Clock skew is an issue exclusive to dynamic logic, whereas clock jitter affects only static CMOS logic networks.
Clock skew can be eliminated by lowering operating frequency, whereas clock jitter is independent of clock frequency and cannot cause hold violations.
Clock skew is caused solely by thermal noise in transistor channels, whereas clock jitter is caused exclusively by lithographic process variations.

questions.question: In a byte-addressable set-associative cache memory, how is a memory address partitioned, and what is the specific operational purpose of the 'Index' field?
options: It determines whether the memory access is decoded as a read operation or a write operation.
It identifies the exact byte or word offset within a stored cache line.
It selects the specific set (row of cache ways) in which the target block may be stored.
It is compared in parallel with stored tags to identify which specific way resulted in a hit.
It specifies the replacement priority among ways using pseudo-LRU algorithms.

questions.question: In Logic Built-In Self-Test (LBIST) architectures for digital ASICs, what is the primary operational role of a Multiple-Input Signature Register (MISR)?
options: To synthesize and apply pseudo-random digital stimulus patterns directly to the combinational logic.
To dynamically detect and correct single-bit soft errors in on-chip SRAM arrays using parity checking.
To measure quiescent power supply leakage current (IDDQ) across scan flip-flops during test pauses.
To compress the multi-bit output response streams from scan chains across test cycles into a compact signature for go/no-go comparison.
To bypass defective scan flip-flops and stitch alternative scan paths via laser-programmable fuses.

questions.question: In modern microprocessor memory hierarchies, Virtually Indexed, Physically Tagged (VIPT) L1 caches allow cache lookup to proceed in parallel with TLB address translation. Under what condition can a VIPT cache suffer from the 'cache synonym' (aliasing) problem?
options: When the virtual address space is strictly smaller than the physical address space.
When the cache line size is smaller than the width of the microprocessor's internal data bus.
When translation lookaside buffer (TLB) misses are serviced purely in software rather than via a hardware page table walker.
When a write-back cache architecture is selected over a write-through cache architecture.
When the size of an individual cache way (total cache capacity divided by associativity) exceeds the virtual memory page size.
